memory_update.text: AXTI is the highest-purity underfollowed candidate for the indium-phosphide export-permit chokepoint: U.S.-listed, mid-cap, AI optical exposure, but China-based production and permit timing create both upside and fragility.
MP should remain the reference anchor for U.S. rare-earth rerouting, but its higher attention level and larger market cap make it less suitable as the main underfollowed discovery candidate.

USAR belongs in the underfollowed lane as a policy-backed mine-to-magnet platform, but survival into later layers requires proof of funding drawdown, customer qualification, commercial production timing, and IP/litigation risk control.

ALOY is a speculative shadow candidate for heavy rare-earth metallization: potentially a very direct policy chokepoint, but claims rely heavily on forward facility execution and must be validated through filings, permits, contracts, and production evidence.

Need a separate pass for graphite, gallium/germanium recyclers, specialty chemical processors, and non-Nasdaq/OTC ADR names such as Metallium or Korea Zinc-linked supply routes; this pass focused on direct U.S.-listed names only.

node: Critical-mineral export controls, permits, and rerouted supply chains
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the policy-rerouting node. The cleanest direct exposure is not only miners but companies whose revenues depend on export permits, non-China processing, rare-earth metallization, magnet capacity, or customer-qualified alternative supply. This pass keeps MP Materials as the obvious reference anchor, while prioritizing AXTI, USAR, and ALOY as more underfollowed or less conventional chokepoint names. No buy/sell view is implied.
